title: Career Roadmap: Charging Infrastructure Engineer
summary: A Charging Infrastructure Engineer designs, installs, tests, and maintains the systems that allow electric vehicles (EVs) to charge safely and reliably. The role connects electrical engineering, power systems, EV technology, renewable energy, communications, and infrastructure planning.

blocks.text: A Charging Infrastructure Engineer designs, installs, tests, and maintains the systems that allow electric vehicles (EVs) to charge safely and reliably. The role connects electrical engineering, power systems, EV technology, renewable energy, communications, and infrastructure planning.

Charging infrastructure engineers may work on residential chargers, commercial charging stations, fleet depots, highway fast-charging hubs, and charging systems integrated with solar power or battery energy storage.
Typical responsibilities

items.text: Assess sites for EV charger installation, electrical capacity, and accessibility.
Select suitable AC or DC chargers based on vehicle types and charging demand.
Design electrical distribution, protection, cabling, earthing, and load management.
Coordinate with utilities, contractors, equipment suppliers, and safety teams.
Commission chargers and troubleshoot electrical, communication, and software faults.
Integrate charging stations with energy management systems, solar PV, and batteries.
Monitor charger uptime, energy consumption, utilization, and maintenance needs.
Follow applicable electrical safety rules, standards, and local regulations.

blocks.label: Career fit
blocks.text: Suitable for students interested in electric vehicles, electrical systems, sustainable mobility, power electronics, and hands-on engineering.
Primary degree
B.Tech / B.E. in Electric Vehicle Technology, Electrical Engineering, Electrical and Electronics Engineering (EEE), or a closely related discipline with EV charging and power-systems coursework.

blocks.label: Typical duration in India
blocks.text: 4 years
Related degree options

Electronics and Communication Engineering, Power Engineering, Energy Engineering, and selected Mechanical Engineering programs with an EV specialization may also be relevant. Electrical design roles often favor candidates with strong electrical engineering fundamentals.
A dedicated EV degree is not the only pathway. For charging infrastructure design, electrical power systems, protection, wiring, and safety are especially important.

blocks.text: Year 1 — Build electrical foundations

items.text: Learn voltage, current, power, energy, AC/DC circuits, and three-phase systems.
Practice circuit analysis and electrical measurements.
Learn basic programming with Python or C for calculations and data analysis.
Develop technical drawing, documentation, and engineering communication skills.
Understand electrical hazards, isolation, and safe laboratory practices.

blocks.label: Target outcome
blocks.text: Ability to explain basic circuits, calculate electrical power, and interpret simple electrical diagrams.
Year 2 — Understand power and EV systems

items.text: Study electrical machines, power electronics, transformers, and power distribution.
Learn battery fundamentals, battery management systems, and EV architecture.
Use circuit simulation tools such as MATLAB/Simulink, LTspice, or equivalent.
Understand fuses, circuit breakers, residual-current protection, earthing, and surge protection.

blocks.label: Target outcome
blocks.text: A documented project comparing charging options and estimating electrical load.
Year 3 — Specialize in charging infrastructure

items.text: Study AC charging, DC fast charging, charging connectors, and communication protocols.
Learn load calculations, cable sizing principles, voltage drop, and demand estimation.
Explore solar PV, battery storage, smart charging, and demand management.
Practice CAD-based electrical layouts and basic energy monitoring.
Seek internships with EV charging companies, electrical contractors, utilities, or energy firms.

blocks.label: Target outcome
blocks.text: A preliminary charging-station design with load calculations, single-line diagram, and safety considerations.
Year 4 — Develop job-ready capability

items.text: Complete a capstone project involving a charging station, fleet depot, or smart charging system.
Learn commissioning procedures, troubleshooting, maintenance, and operational monitoring.
Study the standards and regulatory requirements relevant to the intended job location.
Build a technical portfolio and prepare for electrical design, field engineering, and EV infrastructure interviews.

blocks.label: Target outcome
blocks.text: A documented design project, internship experience where possible, and a clear specialization.

blocks.text: Electrical design tools
AutoCAD or equivalent CAD software, electrical single-line diagrams, cable schedules, load calculations, and site-layout drawings.
Simulation and power systems
MATLAB/Simulink, LTspice, or equivalent tools for understanding converter behavior, load profiles, and electrical-system performance. Specialized power-system software may be useful for grid studies.
Charging networks and monitoring
Learn the concepts behind OCPP-based charger management, charger telemetry, fault logs, remote monitoring, and charging-session data.
Energy analysis
Excel, Python, and Power BI for energy demand estimation, utilization analysis, operating-cost comparisons, and solar-plus-storage assessments.

You do not need to master every tool before applying for internships. Start with electrical calculations, CAD, and Excel; then learn simulation and charger-management platforms according to your chosen role.

sections.heading: Projects to build a strong portfolio

blocks.text: Aim for three or four well-documented projects. Simulation-based projects are suitable for students who do not have access to live charging equipment.

blocks.label: Project 1
blocks.text: EV charging station design
Beginner–Intermediate
Design a hypothetical charging station for a shopping center, office, or residential complex.

blocks.label: Include
blocks.text: Charger selection, number of parking bays, estimated simultaneous demand, preliminary single-line diagram, electrical equipment list, site layout, and safety checklist.

blocks.label: Project 2
blocks.text: AC versus DC charging analysis
Beginner–Intermediate
Compare charging power, approximate charging time, energy requirements, equipment costs, and intended use cases.

blocks.label: Include
blocks.text: Clearly stated assumptions, calculations, comparison charts, and a recommendation for home, workplace, and highway scenarios.

blocks.label: Project 3
blocks.text: Solar-powered EV charging
Intermediate
Estimate how solar generation and battery storage could support charging demand at a workplace or fleet depot.

blocks.label: Include
blocks.text: Hourly load assumptions, solar-generation estimates, storage scenarios, grid-import analysis, and cost trade-offs.

blocks.label: Project 4
blocks.text: Charging network monitoring dashboard
Intermediate–Advanced
Use a synthetic dataset to track charger availability, utilization, energy delivered, charging-session duration, and fault frequency.

blocks.label: Include
blocks.text: A Power BI dashboard, fault classification, utilization trends, and recommendations for improving station uptime.

blocks.label: Portfolio tip
blocks.text: For electrical design projects, document your calculations, assumptions, component ratings, and applicable safety requirements. Do not present a conceptual design as an installation-ready engineering drawing.

blocks.text: Prefer practical courses with assignments and verified syllabi. A short course does not replace a required electrical licence, professional authorization, or employer-specific safety qualification.
Charging infrastructure work is safety-critical. Learn how to identify and apply the current requirements relevant to the project location.
For India, investigate the following areas:

blocks.label: Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS)
blocks.text: Applicable EV charging equipment and connector standards.

blocks.label: Ministry of Power
blocks.text: Current guidelines and requirements for EV charging infrastructure.

blocks.label: Central Electricity Authority (CEA)
blocks.text: Applicable electrical safety and supply regulations.

blocks.label: DISCOM requirements
blocks.text: Sanctioned load, connection approvals, metering, tariffs, and local supply conditions.

blocks.label: National and local building requirements
blocks.text: Fire safety, parking layouts, ventilation where relevant, accessibility, and emergency provisions.

blocks.label: IEC standards
blocks.text: Relevant charging-system, electrical installation, and protection standards as adopted or required for the project.
Requirements can change and vary by site and jurisdiction. Confirm the current applicable versions before designing or commissioning an installation.

A master's degree is not necessary for every entry-level position. Consider postgraduate study when it supports a particular technical specialization or research goal.

By graduation, aim to demonstrate:

items.text: A relevant engineering degree with strong electrical fundamentals.
Understanding of EV charging types, charger selection, and electrical protection.
Ability to prepare and explain a preliminary site layout and single-line diagram.
Working knowledge of CAD and Excel, plus one simulation or analytics tool.
Two or three projects demonstrating design, energy analysis, or troubleshooting.
Internship or field exposure, ideally involving electrical installations or charging infrastructure.
Awareness of relevant Indian electrical safety requirements and charging standards.

blocks.label: Suggested resume headline
blocks.text: EV Charging Infrastructure Engineer | Electrical Design | Power Systems | Smart Charging | Sustainable Mobility

blocks.label: Final recommendation
blocks.text: Start with electrical power systems, protection, and CAD. Then add EV charging technology, commissioning fundamentals, and smart energy management. This combination can prepare you for entry-level opportunities in charging infrastructure, electrical design, field engineering, and charging-network operations.
